# Grid record search: the optional search toolbar and its summary

## Context

This is the toolbar leaf of epic #19791, graduated from #19786 (contracts 4, 5 summary part and 6; options A2, I and J). The operator put the optional toolbar into v13.3 on 2026-10-16. The issues showcase has no text path to Title and Summary, which carry `columnMenu: false`, and a reset means clearing each menu in turn.

## The Problem

A grid cannot offer record search. Nothing shows the filters that have no column header (the search itself, Title and Summary), and nothing clears the grid's own filters in one step.

## The Architectural Reality

- `grid.Container` has no toolbar slot above the header. `footerToolbar_` is a descriptor config that becomes a container item (`src/grid/Container.mjs:151–155`, `:340–342`); it is the precedent.
- `form.field.Search` exists.
- The search contribution, its settings and its validation come from the data-contract leaf of this epic. The toolbar only projects them and writes settings.
- Grid columns declare no `hidden` config, so a "visible columns" scope has no meaning yet. `Body.visibleColumns` is the horizontal viewport range and must never feed the scope.
- Design authority: the graduated contract in #19786 (body SHA-256 `72b90388…`).

## The Fix

- `searchToolbar_` descriptor config on `grid.Container`, mirroring `footerToolbar_`, placed before `headerWrapper`, null by default.
- Search field, a scope selector and a case toggle; clear empties the field. The scope choices are this grid's columns with locked ones included (the default), all record fields, or one column. Labels use the columns' text, never field names. A stored field with no column in this grid reads "Record field: <name>", and only then. A column whose values are neither plain text nor hooked through `fieldText` stays listed as not searchable. "All record fields" says it searches values no column shows. The selector shows the stored field list, so a second toolbar on the same Store shows the same list. (Default set by the author after the operator's design challenge, [D#19786](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19786#discussioncomment-18976022): contract 4 left it open.)
- Summary strip: one removable entry per effective header contribution (`header-inline`, `header-picker`). The search has no entry: its field shows the query, and its clear button empties it while keeping scope and case. Non-removable notes name any restriction the toolbar does not own, a disabled query, an empty resolved scope and a refusal. (Contract 5 delta, ratified on [D#19786](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19786#discussioncomment-18976022) by the author and Emmy.)
- "Clear filters" removes `header-inline`, `header-picker` and `grid-search` by enumeration, never every non-null role and never unowned predicates.
- The issues showcase turns the toolbar on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `searchToolbar_` is null by default, and a grid without it renders unchanged.
- [ ] The scope selector writes the resolved field list, and a second toolbar on the same Store shows that list.
- [ ] The scope defaults to this grid's columns, labelled by column text. A stored field with no column in this grid reads "Record field: <name>". "All record fields" states that it searches values no column shows, and a column without searchable text is listed as not searchable.
- [ ] The summary has no entry for the search; clearing the field keeps scope and case. Header contributions keep removable entries, and a disabled, empty-scope or refused search gets a note.
- [ ] Clear removes only the three UI roles. An independent application predicate survives, and the summary names it.
- [ ] On a narrow grid, the summary exposes every removable state and the reset without widening the grid.
- [ ] The issues showcase reaches Title and Summary through the toolbar in a real browser.
- [ ] A receipt with numbers covers per-keystroke input and row-response latency for literal terms on the 100k `bigData` grid.
- [ ] Grid lifecycle (moved from #19792, which needs no grid): a Store swap, grid destroy and recreate, and two grids on one Store keep or retire the search intent deterministically. Recreating either grid leaves the other's results unchanged.
- [ ] The toolbar writes through `Store#getSearchRefusal()` first and shows its reason instead of writing.

## Out of Scope

Regex (#19786 OQ4), the header active state (the epic's header leaf), the display-policy menu, and the header-filter layout (OQ8).

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-10-16T10:26:19Z

Consumer preparation against producer `e100abcc5051c74298e9564e89a36e6b86486cdc`; no implementation claim yet. The native blocker remains #19792, as Grace reconfirmed.

Prescription checked: `src/grid/Container.mjs` owns toolbar placement and Store reassignment; `src/grid/footer/Toolbar.mjs` supplies the Store-binding precedent, while `src/toolbar/Base.mjs` and `src/form/field/Search.mjs` supply the controls. The new toolbar will project the existing Store contribution through `getFilter(null, 'grid-search')`; attaching, destroying or recreating a grid must not delete or reinterpret that Store-owned intent. Store reassignment changes subscriptions and displayed state. Only an explicit user scope change resolves a new field list, including locked columns, and every write uses `getSearchRefusal` first. Clear enumerates the three admitted UI roles.

The new producer API exposed one integration question: `fields: []` with a nonempty query currently reports effective and excludes every record. Contract 4 requires an inert empty scope with a visible explanation. The exact-source probe was sent to Grace and the existing reviewer Euclid; intrinsic empty-field-set inertness would preserve both the query and any independent application-disabled state. This is being resolved with the producer, not patched around in the toolbar.

The existing five-row oracle remains the functional fixture. Integration coverage will also exercise two differently-columned grids sharing one Store, Store swap/recreate, a retained application predicate, narrow-width summary reachability, the real issues showcase, and measured 100k-row input/response latency.
